key_insight: An AI tool combining pathology slide images with clinical data predicted both chemotherapy response and recurrence risk in HER2-positive early breast cancer across two trial datasets.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help identify patients most likely to benefit from chemotherapy de-escalation while flagging those who may need closer follow-up or more intensive therapy.
method: AI model (ATX NEO) analyzed hematoxylin-eosin whole-slide images plus clinical variables to predict pathological complete response (pCR).
ATX RISK model assessed prognosis and recurrence risk in the PHERGain trial.
Performance was tested in PHERGain and PHERGain-2 using logistic regression, Cox models, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and C-index.
evidence_signal: In evaluable patients, NEO scores were significantly associated with pCR in PHERGain (OR 1.28) and PHERGain-2 (OR 1.30), and RISK score predicted event-free survival in PHERGain (HR 1.56 per 1-SD increase; C-index 0.66).
watch_item: These findings are promising but come from trial cohorts; external validation and practical workflow testing are still needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Predicts Pathological Response and Prognosis in HER2-Positive Early Breast Cancer Treated with Chemotherapy De-escalation Strategies: Analyses from PHERGain and PHERGain-2 Trials
